proof: the client that started the run is dropped while the second model request is in flight; the worker finishes the plan → write → completion on its own — one `RunCreated`, no `RunSuspended`, no `TaskWaiting`, no attention — and a new client reconnecting to the same Core reads the finished task (ReadyForReview / Completed) with the write on disk.
audit: PRESENT since M2/M4 by construction (the run loop lives in the Core under the session lease, checkpoints and the protocol state; a client is a subscriber) and since M6.7 for children; this task adds the explicit qualification. No production code change.
limitations: A desktop-supervised Core exits with its supervising client by design and resumes on the next start (M6.7 covers that path); heartbeats are the lease renewal and capacity ticket renewal per turn.
